title.en: Collective numerals and approximation: дво́е, о́ба, лет пять

card: **дво́е, тро́е, че́тверо…** count people as a group (**нас бы́ло тро́е**), children (**дво́е дете́й**) and nouns that exist only in the plural (**дво́е су́ток**). **о́ба / о́бе** means *both*. Put the number after the noun to say *about*: **лет пять**, *five years or so*.

sections.body: **Два челове́ка** and **дво́е** both mean *two people*, but **нас бы́ло дво́е** (*there were two of us*) is how Russians actually say it. And **о́ба / о́бе** changes with gender, which English *both* doesn't.

head: Numeral
Use
Example
rows: a group of people, men or mixed; children

sections.title: Cases
sections.body: Collective numerals take the genitive plural: **дво́е друзе́й**. In other cases they decline like plural adjectives: **с двои́ми детьми́**, **для обо́их бра́тьев**, **обе́им сёстрам**. They aren't used for women alone: say **три де́вушки**, not ~~тро́е де́вушек~~.

sections.title: Approximation
sections.body: Put the number *after* the noun: **лет пять** (*five years or so*), **часа́ два** (*about two hours*), **челове́к де́сять**. Or use **о́коло** + genitive (**о́коло пяти́ лет**) or **приме́рно** (**приме́рно пять лет**).

mistakes.wrong: Я жил там о́коло пять лет.
mistakes.right: Я жил там о́коло пяти́ лет.

examples.en: I lived there for five years or so.
We drove for about two hours.
